1: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
Green, orange and purple are called secondary colours because you get them by mixing two primary colours.
2: Which Dutch painter painted “The Starry Night”?
Van Gogh painted it in 1889 from his room in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, in the south of France.
3: What is the wooden stand that holds a painter's canvas called?
The word “easel” comes from the Dutch “ezel”, meaning donkey: like a donkey, it carries a load.
4: Which art form uses small pieces of stone or glass to make a picture?
The Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus is famous for its golden mosaics from the 8th century.
5: Which Spanish painter was one of the founders of Cubism?
Picasso invented Cubism with the French painter Georges Braque in the early 20th century.
6: Munch was Norwegian and made several versions of The Scream, the first in 1893.
7: What do you call a painting made on fresh, still-wet wall plaster?
Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in fresco between 1508 and 1512.
8: Which art movement takes its name from a painting by Claude Monet?
The painting “Impression, Sunrise” gave a critic the idea of mockingly calling these artists “Impressionists”.
9: Which Dutch painter painted “Girl with a Pearl Earring”?
The painting, made around 1665, hangs in the Mauritshuis museum in The Hague.
10: Which Flemish painter painted “The Arnolfini Portrait” in 1434?
A small convex mirror at the back of the painting reflects two more figures.
11: Which old painting technique mixes pigments with egg yolk?
Tempera was widely used in the Middle Ages, before oil painting took over.
12: Which collection contains the stories of Aladdin and Ali Baba?
In it, Scheherazade tells a story every night and stops at the most exciting moment.
13: Which little character comes from asteroid B 612?
Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, a pilot, published “The Little Prince” in 1943.
14: Which wooden puppet's nose grows when he lies?
Pinocchio was created by the Italian writer Carlo Collodi in 1881.
15: In the fairy tale, what does Cinderella lose when she leaves the ball?
The prince has every young woman in the kingdom try on the slipper to find Cinderella.
16: What animal is Baloo in “The Jungle Book”?
Bagheera is the black panther and Shere Khan the tiger; Rudyard Kipling wrote the book in 1894.
17: In this Spanish novel published in 1605, the hero mistakes windmills for giants.
18: Which sailor from the Thousand and One Nights makes 7 amazing voyages?
On his voyages, Sinbad meets a giant bird called the roc.
19: Which German brothers collected the tales of Snow White and Hansel and Gretel?
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm published their first collection of tales in 1812.
20: Which Danish writer wrote “The Little Mermaid”?
A statue of the Little Mermaid has sat in Copenhagen harbour since 1913.
21: To which king does Scheherazade tell her stories?
By leaving a story unfinished every evening, Scheherazade saves her life night after night.
22: Which English writer created Robinson Crusoe?
The novel, published in 1719, is said to be inspired by the true story of Scottish sailor Alexander Selkirk.
23: Which Persian poet wrote the “Shahnameh”, the Book of Kings?
This huge epic of more than 50,000 verses was finished around the year 1010.
24: How many strings does a classical guitar have?
An electric bass guitar usually has 4 strings.
25: How many notes are there in the scale do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti?
These note names come from the syllables of a Latin hymn used by the monk Guido of Arezzo in the 11th century.
26: Which family of instruments does the flute belong to?
Bone flutes more than 35,000 years old have been found in Germany.
27: Which bowed string instrument do you hold under your chin?
Violins made by the Italian Antonio Stradivari are among the most valuable instruments in the world.
28: What do you call the person who leads an orchestra?
Conductors often use a small baton to show the musicians the beat.
29: Which Austrian composer wrote the opera “The Magic Flute”?
Mozart composed this opera in 1791, the year he died, aged only 35.
30: Which great composer kept composing after he went deaf?
Beethoven was almost completely deaf when he composed his 9th Symphony.
31: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys.
32: Which fretless string instrument is central to Arabic and Turkish music?
The word “lute” comes from the Arabic “al-ʿūd”.
33: Which Polish composer, nicknamed “the poet of the piano”, lived in Paris?
Chopin wrote almost all of his music for solo piano.
34: Which Indian string instrument did Ravi Shankar make popular in the West?
The sitar has so-called sympathetic strings, which vibrate on their own when the other strings are played.
35: Which German composer wrote the “Brandenburg Concertos”?
Bach dedicated these 6 concertos to the Margrave of Brandenburg in 1721.
36: How many players does a football team have on the pitch?
The goalkeeper is one of those 11 players.
37: How many rings are there in the Olympic symbol?
Pierre de Coubertin designed this symbol in 1913.
38: In which sport do you throw the ball through a hoop?
Basketball was invented in 1891 in the United States by teacher James Naismith.
39: Which sport is played with a racket and a shuttlecock?
In a smash, the shuttlecock can go faster than 400 km/h, making it one of the fastest projectiles in sport.
40: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
The ancient Games were held at Olympia, in honour of the god Zeus.
41: Which Japanese sport's name means “the gentle way”?
Judo was created in 1882 by the Japanese teacher Jigoro Kano.
42: What is the official distance of a marathon?
This odd distance comes from the course of the 1908 London Olympics.
43: How many players does a volleyball team have on the court?
Volleyball was invented in 1895 in the United States by William Morgan.
44: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held, in 1896?
Greece was chosen in honour of the Olympic Games of ancient times.
45: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
A try was only worth 4 points until 1992.
46: In which sport do people talk about a “birdie” and an “eagle”?
A birdie means finishing a hole in 1 stroke under par, an eagle in 2 strokes under.
47: Which men's Olympic event combines 10 athletics disciplines?
For women, the equivalent Olympic event is the heptathlon, with 7 disciplines.
48: Which country does pizza come from?
The Margherita pizza shows the colours of the Italian flag: tomato, mozzarella and basil.
49: Sushi is a signature dish of which country?
The word “sushi” actually refers to the vinegared rice, not the fish.
50: Which Moroccan dish is named after the clay pot with a cone-shaped lid it cooks in?
The cone-shaped lid lets the steam drip back onto the food and keeps it tender.
51: Which tree gives us the beans used to make chocolate?
The Maya and the Aztecs were already drinking cacao more than 1,000 years ago.
52: Which fruit is the main ingredient in guacamole?
Guacamole comes from Mexico, where the Aztecs were already making it.
53: Which country does paella come from?
Paella was born in the Valencia region and is named after the large pan it is cooked in.
54: Which very expensive spice comes from the threads of a crocus flower?
It takes about 150,000 flowers to make 1 kg of saffron.
55: What is the Middle Eastern dip made of chickpeas and tahini called?
Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds.
56: Which country does kimchi, a spicy fermented cabbage, come from?
Making kimchi together, called kimjang, has been on UNESCO's intangible heritage list since 2013.
57: Which Indian bread is baked stuck to the inside wall of a tandoor oven?
A tandoor is a jar-shaped clay oven heated with charcoal.
58: Which pulse is used to make Egyptian falafel, called ta'amiya?
Elsewhere in the Middle East, falafel is usually made with chickpeas.
59: Which country does pho, a rice noodle soup in a fragrant broth, come from?
Pho appeared in the early 20th century in northern Vietnam, around Hanoi.
60: Hebrew and Persian are also written from right to left.
61: How many letters are there in the basic Latin alphabet?
Many languages add letters or accents to this base, like Turkish with ç, ğ and ş.
62: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
Chinese is written with characters that stand for words or syllables, not with an alphabet.
63: What is the writing system of raised dots read by blind people called?
Louis Braille invented it when he was only about 15 years old.
64: What is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet?
Alif is a cousin of the Greek alpha and the Hebrew aleph, which also open their alphabets.
65: Which language does the word “algebra” come from?
It comes from “al-jabr”, a word taken from the title of a book by the scholar al-Khwarizmi in the 9th century.
66: Which ancient people wrote in hieroglyphs?
Jean-François Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in 1822 thanks to the Rosetta Stone.
67: How many letters are there in the Arabic alphabet?
Most Arabic letters change shape depending on where they are in the word.
68: Which alphabet is used to write Russian?
The Cyrillic alphabet is named after Saint Cyril, a 9th-century missionary.
69: Which wedge-shaped writing from Mesopotamia is one of the oldest in the world?
The Sumerians pressed it into clay tablets more than 5,000 years ago.
70: Which people created the alphabet that the Greek, Latin and Arabic alphabets come from?
The Phoenician alphabet had only 22 letters, all consonants.
71: Which alphabet was created in the 15th century by the Korean King Sejong?
King Sejong introduced Hangul in 1446 so that everyone could easily learn to read.
